title: IS12:: arraymin.c (9.3)

lines.code: /* Example: finding minimal value in an array elements
lines.explanation: Comments of the purpose and author of the program should be included in a program.
This is a preprocessor command. System header file stdio.h will be inserted there during compilation.  We include stdio.h header file because it contains function   prototypes for printf and scanf.

The define statement sets up a symbolic constant value for size of the array that is used consistently throughout the program.  For example, wherever N is used, the value 7 will replace it.   Very useful if the value of N needs to be changed.
This is the start of main function definition. Every program should have function main

lines.code: int ar[N]; /* elements from ar[0] to ar[N-1]; */
lines.explanation: An array of 7 integer values is defined.  Because array positions begin from 0, elements of this array have indexes from 0 to 6.

i and min are both declared as integers.  They are integers because min will be storage for the minimum value in the array and i is a counter variable.  A counter variable keeps track of loop iterations.

This loop will execute exactly N times which in this case is 7.  There are 3 parts in the loop header.  The first part initializes the counter variable i to 0.  The second part, i < N;, is the loop conditional. The third is increment ++i.

printf is a standard output function, that in this case takes the value i (the current iteration number) and outputs it.  The % symbol is used to show where the value is to be printed and d is formatting for integers, which i is.
scanf is a standard input function, that in this case takes a value from standard input and stores it into an array element with index i (the memory location 0 to N-1).
End bracket of the for loop.  If a loop contains more than one statement to be executed, denoted by a semi-colon, then brackets are needed to keep all relevant statements together.
The integer variable min is initialized to value of the first element of the array (index 0).

This loop will execute exactly N times which in this case is 7.  There are 3 parts in the loop header.  The first part initializes the counter variable i to 0.  The second part, i < N;, is the loop conditional. The third is increment ++i.

If the value of the condition in the parenthesis is not zero (in C it mean true), then the following statement is executed.  I.e., if the current value of min is greater than the the array lement with index i, then min gets the value of that element.

printf is a standard output function that in this case takes the value min and outputs it.  The % symbol is used to show where the value is to be printed and d is formatting for integers, which min is. The symbol sets the output cursor to the next line
End bracket of main. Brackets are needed to keep all relevant statements together.
